analysis: Changes reviewed: a release version bump in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderCore.swift line 8 (0.10.9 to 0.10.10) and documentation edits in docs/operations/provider-release.md (last-updated date and a rewritten release-description paragraph; the visible head text covers lines 485-1065). No executable security logic changed. The version string feeds registration and packaging, and scripts/check-release-version.sh pins it to the release tag. That script was not supplied, so the match between the tag and the version is unverified. Nothing here alters the attestation, App Attest or serving-authorization paths (TB-009, TB-011, T-054). The release doc describes the dev-branch lane: Developer ID signing, secrets: inherit scoped by environment guards, a source gate that accepts only refs/heads/dev for environment dev, and a ruleset requiring approval and signed commits. These are descriptions of controls in workflow files that were not supplied. The workflow files (release-dev-branch.yml, release-provider.yml, the resume script) were not available, so the claims could not be checked, and they are documentation only. The cluster_runtime block is sent only when the matching *_CLUSTER_RUNTIME_ENABLED variable is true. Registration is described as trusting authenticated pipeline provenance, and official registration does not itself authorize serving, which is consistent with T-052 and T-054. The doc notes that ReleaseVersionGreater is not SemVer, so a dev-branch build can fail to advance the latest alias. That is an operational caveat rather than a security regression. Remaining integration question: whether the .github workflows match the documented secret scoping and branch gating, which this pass did not see. No findings.
